issues.description: Bitmap24::width has different declared types in template vs. solution: template uses `short width;` while solution uses `int width;`. This inconsistency can lead to different range/overflow behavior and warnings, and makes it harder for students to reconcile starter code with the reference implementation (especially since width is used in indexing calculations).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the type of `Bitmap24::width` across template and solution (recommended: use `int width;` in the template to match the solution and typical image dimension ranges).

issues.description: `fix_add_asm` has an inconsistent interface between the NASM implementation and the C test harness: `assignment/fix_add.asm` implements `fix_add_asm` as a 64-bit add that expects four 32-bit stack arguments and returns the 64-bit result in EDX:EAX, while the tests declare and call `fix_add_asm(fix_t, fix_t)` returning a single `fix_t` (with result in EAX). With FIX_LEN=8 (64-bit fix_t), this mismatch breaks the calling convention and makes it impossible to pass the tests without redefining one side.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the `fix_add_asm` ABI consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the NASM `fix_add_asm` to accept exactly two `fix_t` arguments per the tests and return a `fix_t` in the agreed convention, or (B) change the tests/headers to match the current NASM convention (four 32-bit args for a 64-bit add and 64-bit return in EDX:EAX). Ensure the same convention is used everywhere for FIX_LEN=8.
